desktop.notes:
• The offline AI uses the GPU (DirectML: NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) - before, the CPU-only engine was shipped and the GPU sat idle. Each model is tested once in a separate process first; one that a driver cannot run stays on the CPU. AI step alone: 1.3 s → 0.2 s per photo here.
• Each photo is read and decoded once (preview, measuring and AI share it): 30 → 10 MB read per RAW+JPG photo - a third of the disk work (and heat). Camera data from a CR3 reads 256 KB instead of 3 MB.
• Resumes instead of starting over: a folder under a new drive letter or moved elsewhere is recognised (its analysis, AI results and decisions are kept); results are saved as they come; the progress counts photos already done, moves evenly, shows the time left; a run that stops moving restarts and carries on; photos that cannot be read are named. The log says per stage how long it took (Cullect-data/logs).
• Photos moved by hand (Explorer: _saved/_keep → _keep, into _keep / _favourites / _discarded) are recognised: same record, decision from where you put them, nothing analysed again, nothing counted twice. Photos split by an older version get their AI results and favourites back.
• Photo catalog (Tools → Photo catalog): every photo seen, with a tiny picture, its files, where it is now and where it was (folder + drive name) - search "leopard", "silhouette", "birds", a place, a name - also when that card or drive is not connected.
• Send to RapidRAW (right-click; RapidRAW is found automatically, Settings → General picks another editor): opens the photo there - the RAW of a RAW+JPG pair for RAW editors. Nothing is moved or changed.
• Full screen (Space) returns to exactly the window you had - maximized stays maximized, a window gets its size and place back.
• A folder that is gone (card out, moved) is never recreated by saving its .cullect file.
